page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Margin notes on the right, beside the first lines of the column. Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.l: Si voluntas est absoluta, tum Deus decreto
absoluto determinavit omnes liberas conver-
siones omnium electorum, & per eandem
rationem omnes etiam liberas non-conversio-
nes reproborum. Ferrum prius quam hoc de-
coxerit Itomachus[?] Jesuiticus aut. Arminianus.
O jam tollitur (inquiunt) libertas, everti-
tur omnis religio, introducitur fatum, Stoi-
cismus, Manechismus, & quid non? Suis
hic opitulari cupit Grevinchov. ita etiam &
nobile ingenium Petri Fonsecae. Omnia vo-
lunt reduci ad decretum absolutum, ut in
causam altissimam. Ita enim illi, si Petrus
in hisce & non in aliis occasionibus & rerum
ordine collocabitur, & tali modo dispositus
vocabitur, tum obsequetur divinae vocationi.
Sed ego decerno (inquit Deus) absolute
collocare Petrum in tali rerum ordine, &
ipsum tali modo dispositum vocare. Ergo
absoluta mea voluntas prima est causa, cur Pe-
trus meae obsequatur vocationi. Sed Resp.
2. Non est hic primus & altissimus ille syllo-
gismus in quem reducetur tota vocationis ef-
ficacia, 1. Major non est necessaria, imo stan-
te indifferentia Jesuitica & Arminiana in
voluntate Petri, non magis vera quam falsa, &
falsa, quam vera est major propositio conne-
xa. Nam in quocunque rerum ordine collo-
cetur Petrus, nunquid ille ordo ipsius vo-
luntatem ad assentiendem Dei vocationi de-
terminabit? Num quaefo tantum convivium,
mens hilaris, timor aliquis gehennae aut ejus-
modi

page.notes: Tit. 216 is hard to read in the margin; the number after it may be 216 or 2i6. The running head and page number are set in spaced small capitals and are partly unclear. "Itomachus" is uncertain. The word "Stoicismus" was read from a long-s form. The final line ends the page and runs into the catchword "modi". Shows some show-through from the opposite side, which was not transcribed.
